images.title: Axes, scale and bars
images.purpose: Show the three parts of a bar graph drawing: two perpendicular lines, an equal-step scale on the vertical line, and bars of equal width.
images.composition: One large L-shaped pair of axes centred on a plain white page, three bars inside, one label on each axis and one scale note; lots of empty space.
images.exact_structure: Two perpendicular grey #6B7280 lines (horizontal and vertical). Vertical line has exactly 6 equal-spaced tick marks above the corner. Exactly 3 bars of identical width with equal gaps: first teal #0072B2 height 3 steps, second amber #E69F00 height 5 steps, third teal height 2 steps. Bars stand on the horizontal line. No grid, no numbers on ticks. Exactly 3 bars, 6 ticks, 2 axes.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
bars of different widths, uneven gaps or uneven tick spacing
images.takeaway: A bar graph needs two lines, an equal-step scale and bars of the same width.
images.description: A simple bar graph frame: horizontal and vertical lines, 6 equal ticks, and 3 equal-width bars of heights 3, 5 and 2 steps.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the two lines, the equal steps and the equal-width bars, and say what each is for.

image_decisions.why: The drawing steps (axes, scale, bars) are best shown as one clean graph frame.
